definitions.explanation: Eating eagerly by repeatedly opening and closing the mouth; wolfing down food.
The motion of a mouth (or mouth-like thing) repeatedly opening and closing.

examples.japanese: ⟦おにぎり→おにぎり：04956_onigiri⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ぱくぱく⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
⟦{子|こ}ども→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ケーキ→ケーキ：01356_keeki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ぱくぱく⟦{食|た}べた→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: The child gobbled up the cake.

examples.japanese: ⟦おなか→お腹：00805_onaka⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦すいていた→すく：00756_suku⟧⟦ので→ので：09501_node⟧、⟦お{弁当|べんとう}→弁当：01014_bentou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ぱくぱく⟦{頬張|ほおば}った→頬張る：14618_hoobaru⟧。
examples.english: I was hungry, so I wolfed down my lunchbox.

examples.japanese: ⟦{金魚|きんぎょ}→金魚：00233_kingyo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ぱくぱく⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: The goldfish is opening and closing its mouth.

examples.japanese: ⟦{赤|あか}ちゃん→赤ちゃん：01282_akachan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{口|くち}→口：00560_kuchi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ぱくぱく⟦{動|うご}かしている→動かす：01885_ugokasu⟧。
examples.english: The baby is moving its mouth open and shut.
The carp that surfaced was opening and closing its mouth.

notes:
An onomatopoeia representing the repeated opening and closing of the mouth, either while eating eagerly or as a standalone mouth motion.

SOUND SYMBOLISM:
The voiceless 「ぱ」 suggests light, quick movements, giving a cute or childlike impression. Contrast with ⟦がつがつ→がつがつ：05936_gatsugatsu⟧, which sounds rougher and greedier.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ぱくぱく⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧: to munch, gobble up
- ⟦{口|くち}→口：00560_kuchi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ぱくぱく: opening and closing one's mouth
- ぱくぱく⟦{頬張|ほおば}る→頬張る：14618_hoobaru⟧: to stuff one's cheeks

RELATED EATING ONOMATOPOEIA:
- ⟦もぐもぐ→もぐもぐ：05775_mogumogu⟧: chewing (mouth closed, quiet eating)
- ⟦がつがつ→がつがつ：05936_gatsugatsu⟧: eating greedily (rough, rude image)
- ⟦ぱくっと→ぱくっと：noentry⟧: taking one big bite (single action)
- ⟦むしゃむしゃ→むしゃむしゃ：07434_mushamusha⟧: munching noisily
